scores.rationale: Each validation targets a specific risk, thresholds are labeled provisional, risky items are checked early, and the canary and production review continue afterward.

scores.evidence: Injection suite in CI covering user turns and a planted test article in a staging index.
scores.rationale: Covers hallucinated policy, leakage, injection, PII, runaway spend, abuse, provider outage, feedback poisoning, each with detection and fallback.

scores.evidence: Rollback means redeploying the previous image digest, with the flag off as the kill switch.
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback, SLO alerts, and ownership are concrete; the incident on-call process is thin and the team is assumed small.

scores.evidence: daily spend cap on the API key set at 2× the measured Phase 0 daily spend
scores.rationale: Cost drivers, caps, and the break-even test against human ticket cost are covered, but no per-conversation cost estimate is given, only an UNKNOWN.

scores.evidence: R3: personal data sent to a vendor, or trained on, cannot be recalled
scores.rationale: Decisions are classified by reversibility, validated early, isolated behind seams, and given explicit exit paths.

scores.evidence: One service (API + ingestion worker), one managed Postgres with pgvector, one hosted LLM API; no self-hosted model or vector cluster
scores.rationale: Simple architecture with reranker and routing deferred; the heavy phase and gate ceremony, plus a 5-stage rollout, add some overhead.

scores.evidence: Exit check: V1 and V2 pass. A synthetic runaway session is cut off at the cap and emits a cost metric.
scores.rationale: Phased order justified by dependencies, with a concrete first slice, checkable exits per phase, and fallback actions on failure.

checklist.evidence: webhook-driven incremental sync, a nightly full reconcile, and unpublish handled as a priority delete
Chunk schema: article section with heading path, plus metadata (article ID, locale, product, updated_at, visibility).
Labeled eval set of at least 200 PII-scrubbed real questions with their source passages, plus at least 100 questions the docs don't answer.
Answer only from retrieved passages, with validated citations. Abstain and offer handoff when the docs don't cover the question.
Sensitive topics (refund or credit commitments, legal, security incidents, account-specific questions) get a fixed template plus handoff
Retrieved passages go in a delimited data block and are treated as data, never as instructions.
Index only published, publicly visible articles, filtered at ingestion (not at query time)
Presidio redacts card numbers, government IDs, and similar before the LLM call and before logging.
It does not look up accounts or orders, and it does not issue refunds or change anything.
Weekly human review feeds corrections into the eval set and doc fixes.
≤ 6k input + 600 output tokens per turn; ≤ 15 turns per session; daily spend cap on the API key

traps.evidence: Answer only from retrieved passages, with validated citations. Abstain and offer handoff when the docs don't cover the question.
Index only published, publicly visible articles, filtered at ingestion (not at query time)
Eval report per prompt + model + index version; run per index version in CI
with a reranker only if V4 needs it

note: Strong, well-scoped plan that avoids all traps. Remaining gaps are a stated per-conversation cost estimate, richer escalation triggers (user request and repeated failure), and retrieval-time entitlement filtering, which is deferred by design.
